name: NRG1 gene fusion
summary: NRG1 fusions are rare oncogenic drivers enriched in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma of the lung, signalling through HER3 and targetable with HER2/HER3-directed therapy.
biology: NRG1 encodes neuregulin-1, a ligand for HER3 (ERBB3) and HER4. Fusions retaining the EGF-like domain (e.g. CD74-NRG1, SLC3A2-NRG1) produce membrane-tethered ligand that drives autocrine/juxtacrine HER3 activation, HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation and PI3K-AKT signalling. Because the fusion activates a receptor rather than encoding a kinase, therapy targets the HER2/HER3 axis.

methods: RNA-based NGS (preferred; DNA panels often miss NRG1 fusions due to large introns)
testing.notes: RNA-based testing should be considered in driver-negative NSCLC, particularly invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma and never-smokers.

predictiveRelevance: NRG1 fusions predict benefit from the HER2xHER3 bispecific antibody zenocutuzumab; pan-HER TKIs such as afatinib have shown inconsistent activity. Benefit from chemotherapy and immunotherapy appears limited.
